Keep the incumbent transform intact until a replacement reproduces every available pair; do not overwrite it with a guess or placeholder.

For repeated grids, identify period and phase independently on each axis and determine whether output samples cells, intersections, or regions and includes boundaries. For tilings or reflections, verify quadrant orientations and row/column placement against full examples—not just a few rows or a presumed symmetry. Treat all mappings as hypotheses and test them on every demo, especially examples with different orientations or crop sizes. For fill/region rules, compare 4-neighbor and diagonal connectivity against every demo, including edge-touching pockets. Identify which pixels are boundary markers, seeds, and background; test the hypothesized propagation direction, stopping conditions, and treatment of marker pixels against examples with different orientations. Never infer that a marker changes color or that a region fills merely from a failed submission.

Submit only the test grid serialized directly from that run—never transcribe or repair it manually. Keep temporary runner data in the workspace, not `/tmp`.
4. On each turn take exactly one task action (`submit`, `request_demos`, or, after the instance is over, `finish`) and put its JSON object on the final line.
